turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your attempts at provocation are noted, Sandip. I am not easily intimidated, and your insinuations regarding my standing are irrelevant to the matter at hand. Let us proceed to the issue of your activities amongst my tenants, as they are of considerably more import.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: It seems we are all rather... agitated. Perhaps a moment of quiet would allow us to consider the gravity of these accusations before responding with further heat?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, quiet, you say, Bimala? A most agreeable suggestion, though one suspects it’s born less of genuine serenity and more of a desire to forestall the inevitable unraveling of… well, let’s just say *difficult* truths. Tell me, Nikhil, do you truly believe a moment of silence can erase the whispers that follow a man who allows his tenants to be exploited?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, you speak of whispers, but are they truly so dangerous, or merely uncomfortable? Perhaps it is discomfort that Nikhil wishes to avoid, not necessarily a concealment of truth. I believe a little discomfort can be… clarifying.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The discomfort you describe, Bimala, is not the concern. It is the potential for injustice and the disruption of order that warrant attention. I suggest you both focus your energies on constructive action, rather than indulging in rhetorical flourishes.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Constructive action, you say? How very…noble, Nikhil. But tell me, does one build a house with only the best intentions? I find that a certain degree of… *force*, shall we say, is required to move the stones, wouldn't you agree?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Force, Sandip? Such a… blunt word. I wonder if it is truly necessary, or if sometimes, a gentle persuasion, a well-placed understanding, can achieve a more lasting effect?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A gentle persuasion, you say, Bimala? How charmingly naive. I daresay, sometimes a firm hand is required to guide those who stray from the path – and I fear, my dear Nikhil, that your tenants are straying rather far afield. One simply cannot rely on the benevolence of the lost.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies are… unproductive, Sandip. My tenants are under my protection, and any accusations of their deviation require verifiable evidence, not conjecture. I trust you understand the distinction.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Verifiable evidence, you say? How refreshingly pragmatic, Nikhil. But tell me, do you truly believe that all dangers announce themselves with a signed affidavit? Sometimes, the shadows lengthen before the storm breaks, and it requires a certain… *discernment*, wouldn’t you agree, to see them?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Shadows…yes, they can be deceptive. But are we not also sometimes blinded by our own assumptions, Nikhil? Perhaps what you perceive as shadows, others see as merely the play of light.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My concern is not with interpretations of shadows, Sandip, but with the well-being of those entrusted to my care. If you possess genuine information regarding my tenants’ behavior, I request you present it directly to me, rather than employing such veiled insinuations. Otherwise, I must ask you to address your concerns elsewhere.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, verifiable evidence! A most… *pedestrian* demand, Nikhil. Do you recall Shelley’s *Ozymandias*, my dear fellow? The ruins spoke volumes, yet where was the signed affidavit proclaiming the king’s hubris? One might argue that some truths are best apprehended through a more… *intuitive* faculty, wouldn't you agree?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Intuition is a fascinating thing, Sandip, but it can also be a treacherous guide if left unchecked. Is it not possible, then, that *all* of us, regardless of our perceived wisdom, are susceptible to misinterpretations, to seeing what we *wish* to see?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Bimala, my dear, you possess a certain… *acute* understanding of the human condition, a sensitivity that I find quite admirable. But tell me, is it not also true that unchecked intuition can become a breeding ground for paranoia? A fertile field for whispers and anxieties, particularly when one's safety—and, dare I say, one's *influence*—is at stake?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Paranoia… it’s a heavy cloak to wear, Sandip. But perhaps it is not always born of fear, but of a desperate search for clarity in a world shrouded in deliberate obscurity. I wonder, are we truly safer when we choose to ignore the shadows, or merely more comfortable?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A desperate search for clarity, you say? How exquisitely put, Bimala! But clarity, alas, is often the casualty of those who cling too tightly to their illusions. Tell me, are you so certain that the shadows you perceive are merely shadows, and not the vanguard of a storm?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: A storm, Sandip? Such dramatic pronouncements are easily made, but the true measure of a man lies not in predicting tempests, but in weathering them. I find myself pondering, though, whether the shadows are cast *by* the storm, or whether they themselves *create* it.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Indeed, a most intriguing proposition, Bimala. But tell me, does one truly *weather* a storm by merely contemplating its nature? Or does one, perhaps, require a sturdy vessel, a capable crew, and a certain… understanding of the currents that drive it? I suspect, Nikhil, you possess such a vessel, though whether you’re willing to navigate the turbulent waters remains to be seen.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's inquiries are becoming tiresome. I am not concerned with Bimala’s musings on storms or vessels, nor with your veiled assessments of my capabilities; I am concerned with the well-being of my household and those under my protection, and I expect you to address that concern with the same directness you seem to deny me.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
